A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AudioMCQ and audio-contribution-aware post-training study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original silent-audio evaluations, dataset analyses, and Qwen2.5-Omni training experiments, including Tables 2–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, revises the Mixed-to-Strong results, and adds checkpoint-selection trajectories in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation pipeline, three-model majority-vote filtering, Qwen2.5-Omni backbone, and SFT/GRPO training paradigms remain the same. The added pipeline-verification description documents checks without establishing that the underlying construction procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven source datasets and evaluate MMAU-test-mini, MMAU, MMAR, and MMSU, retaining the silent-audio and strong-audio-contribution analyses. RUListening is newly cited but is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the silent-audio comparisons and Table 5. Adding the label 'backbone' to Qwen2.5-Omni clarifies its role without introducing a different comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported Mixed-to-Strong checkpoint from 1,000 SFT plus 900 GRPO steps to 1,000 plus 500. The checkpoint-selection criterion, data controls, and appendix's 1,000-step RL phase remain unchanged; this does not establish a rerun or reduced total training budget.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 shows how MMAU-test-mini-4k validation accuracy varies across intermediate training checkpoints and identifies the selected checkpoints. The existing strong-audio-contribution comparison and zero-audio case studies are retained, with the former moved from v1 Figure 4 to v3 Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added checkpoint trajectories do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: For the revised Mixed-to-Strong checkpoint, Table 5 changes MMAU-test-mini/MMAU/MMAR/MMSU scores from 75.8/74.6/67.1/70.7 to 76.4/75.1/67.0/71.7. Table 8 updates corresponding subgroup scores and averages, and Figure 4 adds validation results. Other methods' table scores remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same dataset transformations, audio-contribution definition, filtering rule, and GRPO objective. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same contributions: AudioMCQ, identification and filtering of text-answerable questions, and the Weak-to-Strong and Mixed-to-Strong paradigms. The benchmark leadership and DCASE claims retain their scope despite the revised headline numerical results.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets improvements as gains in perception capability, particularly on MMAR and MMSU, and drops the explicit characterization of Mixed-to-Strong's MMAU performance as suboptimal. The conclusion adds more robust audio-contribution partitioning as a future direction.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents format checking, iterative regeneration, spot-checking by 2–3 annotators, and prompt/checker refinement. Section 4 explicitly discloses CoT exclusion from evaluation. Existing prompts and hyperparameters remain substantively unchanged, while the footnote identifying specific unreleased baselines is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zang et al.'s RUListening work and contrasts its Gaussian-noise replacement with this study's silent-audio input in Section 3.1. The remaining research positioning is retained; the Audio-Thinker reference change is bibliographic.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, adds the quality-verification appendix and acknowledgements, and updates cross-references, author text, affiliations, and publication headers. Most methodological exposition, prompts, and case-study text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a two-panel checkpoint-selection figure and moves the six-panel performance comparison from the appendix into Section 4.2 as Figure 5, with updated axes and caption. Figures and tables are resized or repositioned, including a larger appendix Table 8, while the overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency through Appendix C's construction-check details, explicit CoT exclusion, and Figure 4's checkpoint-selection evidence. Bringing the strong-audio-contribution comparisons into the main text also improves accessibility. These gains outweigh the less specific baseline-sourcing footnote; the revised scores use a different checkpoint and do not independently establish a same-setting performance improvement.
